The shop windows are a bit damaged.”NFL closes Paris storeThe NFL pop-up store in Paris will be closed on Saturday, the league said on Friday.Monika Allen, a 56-year-old Steelers fan, was on her way to the shop on Friday to buy “more Steelers clothes”, saying she “didn’t prepare for the cold and the wind”.The unrest is not the only thing that has disrupted the build-up to the game, with Storm Austen hitting parts of the country. Météo-France, the national weather agency, has issued orange alerts for much of the country’s north-west, including the Paris region.The Steelers landed in France on Friday morning. They were due to practise at the Stade de France before holding a press conference.They eventually cancelled their training session because of bad weather, and the press conference was moved to their hotel in Paris.The Saints have been practising this week in Versailles after arriving in France on Monday.“Due to elevated wind and rain conditions, in accordance with local authorities, there will not be a media viewing portion during today’s Saints practice,” the Saints said in a statement.The NFL also cancelled a fan event on Friday.“NFL Experience Paris presented by Wilson is closed for the rest of today due to adverse weather. Please do not attend the site,” the NFL said in a statement.Explore more on these topicsNFLAaron RodgersPittsburgh SteelersNew Orleans SaintsParisFranceUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: World Series 2026 predictions: will the Rays or Brewers claim their first title? | World Series | The Guardian
description: It’s Milwaukee and Tampa Bay in the 122nd Fall Classic. Our writers predict how it will be decided, who will shine brightest and who will break their World Series maiden
Author: Alan Evans
Headline: It’s Milwaukee and Tampa Bay in the 122nd Fall Classic. Our writers predict how it will be decided, who will shine brightest and who will break their World Series maiden
Content: The Rays and Brewers are both aiming for their first World Series title.Composite: Guardian Pictures; MLB Photos/Getty Images; Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe Rays and Brewers are both aiming for their first World Series title.Composite: Guardian Pictures; MLB Photos/Getty Images; Getty ImagesWorld SeriesWorld Series 2026 predictions: will the Rays or Brewers claim their first title?It’s Milwaukee and Tampa Bay in the 122nd Fall Classic. Our writers predict how it will be decided, who will shine brightest and who will break their World Series maidenAlan Evans,Bryan Armen GrahamandDavid LengelFri 23 Oct 2026 04.00 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIs this World Series proof that money doesn’t bring (baseball) happiness?Yes- and in fact, evidence that money actively undermines baseball happiness. For the big-market teams, anything less than a World Series is disappointing. Whereas for the Rays (who in Aprilwere given a 1.1% chance of winning the World Seriesby FanGraphs) or Brewers (2.1%), the season is already a success, and winning it all would give their fans more pleasure than a Yankees or Dodgers fan couldeverexperience.Alan EvansNo.It’s does offer proof that October remains gloriously resistant to being bought outright. But money buys depth and insurance, even if it can’t guarantee that your $300m hitters won’t spend an off week grounding into double plays. Better to enjoy this peach of a matchup – only the second Fall Classic since 1920 where a first-time winner is guaranteed – without letting baseball’s billionaire owner class weaponize it in the coming labor fight, with a salary cap on the table and the sport potentially heading for another protracted lockout.Bryan Armen GrahamYes.High-end talent is nice, but to get to theWorld Serieson a shoestring budget you also need a certain culture. There shall be no tolerating careless mistakes, no getting too comfortable in cushy MLB dugouts, and players must have a clear understanding of their roles and the brand of baseball they’re expected to play. That’s where Milwaukee and Tampa Bay have truly excelled this season.David LengelQuick GuideWorld Series 2026ShowScheduleBest-of-seven series. All times US Eastern Daylight Time (EDT).Fri 23 OctGame 1: Tampa Bay at Milwaukee, 8pm (Fox)Sat 24 OctGame 2: Tampa Bay at Milwaukee, 8pm (Fox)Mon 26 OctGame 3: Milwaukee at Tampa Bay, 8pm (Fox)Tue 27 OctGame 4: Milwaukee at Tampa Bay, 8pm (Fox)Wed 28 OctGame 5: Milwaukee at Tampa Bay, 8pm* (Fox)Fri 30 OctGame 6: Tampa Bay at Milwaukee, 8pm* (Fox)Sat 31 OctGame 7: Tampa Bay at Milwaukee, 8pm* (Fox)*-if necessaryHow to watchIn the US, all World Series games will air on Fox and Fox Deportes, with streaming available through Fox One. In the UK, the series will be carried by TNT Sports. In Australia, fans can watch on ESPN, with streaming available through Disney+ and Kayo Sports.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.What the Brewers need to do to winJacob Misiorowski may be the best pitcher in the world, but the cliché that“bullpens win championships”is more true than ever in modern baseball. Luckily for Milwaukee, theirs is one of the best in the game – only the Yankees had a better collective regular season earned run average – and the sweep of the Dodgers means everyone will be starting on full rest.AEMake Tampa Bay chase.Milwaukee have the pitching to win this series, but asking them to weather seven nights of high-leverage situations with traffic on the basepaths is inviting trouble. Get ahead in counts, limit free passes and force the Rays to string hits together. The fewer opportunities Tampa Bay have to improvise, the better the Brewers’ chances.BAGThe Brewers bullpen is lights out but don’t ask them to do too much.The Rays will try to pile up reliever innings in a bid to weaken the core. Also, Game 4 in Tampa will be a bullpen game for Milwaukee, so make sure the unit is kept fresh for that pivotal matchup.DLView image in fullscreenJacob Misiorowski has enjoyed a breakout season with the Milwaukee Brewers, emerging as one of baseball’s most exciting young pitchers and helping propel the team to the World Series.Photograph: John Fisher/Getty ImagesWhat the Rays need to do to winBe inventive.Ace Shane McClanahan is injured, but their occasional gambit of using opening pitchers is arguably even more of a power move in a single series at the very end of the season. As for batting, if any two of the “big three” of Yandy Díaz, Jonathan Aranda and Junior Caminero find their groove at the same time, they’ll be hard to keep quiet.AETurn every baserunner into a problem.Swipe a bag, take the extra base and make Milwaukee’s fielders execute under pressure. But don’t confuse small ball with giving away outs: Díaz, Aranda and Caminero still need to supply damage. The best version of the Rays makes opponents defend everything, including the outfield seats.BAGEnsure the big three are up and running against the Brewers rotation.When Caminero, Díaz and Aranda struggled in the ALCS, the Guardians took two games and sent Rays fans searching for the nearest cliff. Kevin Cash also must excel in the dugout against healthy competition in Pat Murphy, who won’t make Dave Roberts-like mistakes.DLOne bold predictionTampa Bay will clinch the title wearing their Devil Rays throwback jerseys, and within a year will revert to that as the franchise name.They went 12-3 in the regular season wearing them and are now 2-0 in the postseason. If it happens, fan demand will make it hard for the newish owners to resist.AESomeone will lose a game after pulling a starter who looks untouchable, and the ensuing argument will briefly eclipse the actual World Series. The manager will point to the matchups, the broadcast will show the abandoned pitcher staring into space and everyone will pretend the alternative outcome was a matter of certainty. (And for Tampa Bay fans,it could be déjà vu.)BAGClub Tropicanaby Wham! becomes the theme song for the Rays and this World Series as the dumpy dome in St Pete becomes the epicenter of the October sports world. Tampa win in seven tight games and fall in love with the worst venue in all of Major League Baseball.They take a 180 turn on the Trop and demand that their new owners drop plans for a new stadium.Talk about bold!DLView image in fullscreenJunior Caminero’s prodigious power has been a driving force behind the Tampa Bay Rays’ remarkable postseason run, with the young slugger delivering another standout campaign at the heart of their lineup.Photograph: Julio Aguilar/Getty ImagesWorld Series MVPChandler Simpson, Tampa Bay.He’s become the talisman of a team increasingly focused on small ball, and is well on his way to becoming a folk hero for his homer-averse approach. Tight games are often decided by small margins such as a stolen base or a timely bunt. If it happens two or three times at key moments, the underdog could finally have his day.AEJunior Caminero, Tampa Bay.There’s a temptation to choose someone whose candidacy explains the Rays’ entire organizational philosophy. I’ll take the less complicated option: the hitter who can put the ball into the seats with thepurist-rankling, time-expanding home-run trot. In a series of infinitesimal margins, one emphatic swing can turn the whole thing.BAGDrew Rasmussen, Tampa Bay.Like Freddy Peralta, Drew Rasmussen has spent some time in a Brewers jersey, and has benefited from whatever they’re sprinkling on pitchers in Tampa. The 31-year-old righty was a sixth-round pick who can miss bats and hit his spots with ease. In this World Series, he will reach the pinnacle.DLYour winner will be ...Rays 4-3 Brewers.There’s not much between the teams, but the Rays have surpassed every expectation this season and easily won the toughest division in baseball. It’s close to a tossup, but the Rays’ versatility and Cash’s managerial nous might be enough to edge it.AERays 4-3 Brewers.Milwaukee have the pitching to make every run feel precious, but I trust the Rays’ ability to manufacture offense to make the difference in a series where margins will be razor-thin. There’s something about this matchup that reminds me of the 1991 World Series between the Twins and Braves: Great Lakes v South, two evenly matched teams with no obvious weaknesses and barely a whisker between them. Expect seven games of mounting tension, managerial second-guessing and repeated reminders that neither of these teams arrived here by accident.BAGRays 4-3 Brewers.How could it not go seven? They’re so close in culture and approach that you’d be shocked if either of these teams went down without a fight. The Rays have just a little bit more, and a slight advantage at skipper with Kevin Cash. It’ll be super tight: Rays in seven.DLExplore more on these topicsWorld SeriesMilwaukee BrewersTampa Bay RaysBaseballUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Enciso rescues point in storm for Ipswich to deny Nottingham Forest | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Julio Enciso equalised Neco Williams’s goal to give Ipswich a 1-1 draw with Nottingham Forest at Portman Road
Author: John Brewin
Headline: Julio Enciso equalised Neco Williams’s goal to give Ipswich a 1-1 draw with Nottingham Forest at Portman Road
Content: Julio Enciso slots in Ipswich’s equaliser.Photograph: Keeran Marquis/SPP/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenJulio Enciso slots in Ipswich’s equaliser.Photograph: Keeran Marquis/SPP/ShutterstockPremier LeagueEnciso rescues point in storm for Ipswich to deny Nottingham ForestJohn Brewinat Portman RoadFri 23 Oct 2026 17.07 EDTLast modified on Fri 23 Oct 2026 18.51 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAmid a Suffolk squall, winds whipping, a constant drum of rain, an encounter full of half-chances, mistakes, the obligatory refereeing controversy and searching questions. Do Ipswich possess the stones to deal with the big league? Perhaps so. How long can Nottingham Forest’s dip sustain before their president, Evangelos Marinakis, takes his usual course of action. Perhaps not much longer.Ipswich’s Gary O’Neil was the happier manager, Forest had created the cleaner opportunities, only for familiar failings to cost them. “We were never quite good enough with the ball to turn it into a football match,” said O’Neil. Further adding to Forest’s disappointment, Ipswich’s Issa Diop escaped what looked, on first glance, a red card for a last-man foul. A first-half exchange of goals, both owing much to defensive laxness, determined the result.Ipswich 1-1 Nottingham Forest: Premier League – liveRead moreIpswich’s aim is to establish themselves as Forest have in the Premier League. Though Forest and their manager cannot be presumptive of their statuses. “The result doesn’t reflect the performance but I don’t see another solution other than to keep going,” said Oliver Glasner. Forest havesix points from eight matches, just a single win.Glasner admitted he is still “waiting for this click” while saying: “I see great togetherness. The spirit I start to feel … I loved everything I saw today, just not the result.” A record of starting slow only to flourish at previous clubs offers partial protection, though Forest’s ownership is not like other clubs’. Wednesday was the anniversary of Sean Dyche’s appointment. That tenure lasted just 100 days.Liam Delap’s presence in the Forest ranks, the striker barracked at every touch by home fans, served as a reminder of Ipswich’s failed mission two seasons ago. Unloved in Ipswich for decamping to Chelsea, Delap continues to be short of the confidence he showed back then.Forest kicked off as lowest scorers in the division; no side had drawn a blank more often. Their drought did not take long to break but no flood followed. Neco Williams’s goal came via an overlap and then a looping cross from Daniel Muñoz. Williams glided in unmarked, his finish low and true beyond Christian Walton.Another Forest goal appeared likely before home fans, previously exasperated, were lifted by Jaden Philogene forcing a save from Matz Sels and Julio Enciso dancing through red shirts to force another.The equaliser came via a collective loss of concentration characteristic of Forest’s season so far, echoing defeat at Crystal Palace, and at home to Coventry. Jair Cunha gallivanted forward and, adrenaline coursing, lost possession. Dara O’Shea’s punted clearance was poorly dealt with by Nikola Milenkovic, an under-amped back-pass allowed Enciso to show admirable calm when others had surrendered theirs.Forest’s failure to claim the rewards on offer from the first half told a familiar story. So too do repeated refereeing controversies, and howls of conspiracy among their supporters. How the officials, led by Thomas Bramall, the referee, did not view Diop’s clattering of James McAtee as a foul defied belief. Play was waved on. More understandable, if still highly debatable, was the verdict via video assistant that McAtee had conceded possession with a heavy touch as the collision came. “Leif [Davis] was there to cover,” said Diop, shown a yellow card. “I don’t think it’s a red.”“I think they came to the right conclusion, a good process,” O’Neil said. As well he might. “It looks like the VAR was not from the East Midlands today,” said Glasner. “It felt like it was a red card.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionInjustice fuelled Forest though did not make them any more clinical, the best of their second-half flurry of chances involved Murillo missing a free header from a corner. That asked for staying power from Ipswich. So far this season, they have not been the soft touch under O’Neil they became in Kieran McKenna’s survival attempt. “We had to show another side to get something,” said O’Neil. “We can play better but if we think we’re going to be dominant in every game … we’ll be fighting for scraps a lot of the time.”Luck was definitely ridden. Callum Hudson-Odoi, as eight messy minutes of injury time were being added, received more than enough time and space to do far better than drag beyond the far post. The story of the night encapsulated for Forest. And of their season.View image in fullscreenNeco Williams runs off in triumph after giving Forest the lead.Photograph: Richard Heathcote/Getty ImagesExplore more on these topicsPremier LeagueIpswich TownNottingham Forestmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Connor Hellebuyck traded to New Jersey as Winnipeg Jets end bitter standoff with US Olympic hero | New Jersey Devils | The Guardian
description: The three-time Vezina winner joins Olympic teammate Jack Hughes in New Jersey after a months-long standoff with Winnipeg that included a suspension
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The three-time Vezina winner joins Olympic teammate Jack Hughes in New Jersey after a months-long standoff with Winnipeg that included a suspension
Content: Connor Hellebuyck and members of the US men’s Olympic hockey team wave to the crowd during Donald Trump’s State of the Union address at the US Capitol in Washington on 24 February 2026.Photograph: Chip Somodevilla/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenConnor Hellebuyck and members of the US men’s Olympic hockey team wave to the crowd during Donald Trump’s State of the Union address at the US Capitol in Washington on 24 February 2026.Photograph: Chip Somodevilla/Getty ImagesNew Jersey DevilsConnor Hellebuyck traded to New Jersey as Winnipeg Jets end bitter standoff with US Olympic heroThree-time Vezina winner leaves Winnipeg after 11 yearsDevils send four players and two draft picks to JetsOlympic gold medalist joins US teammate Jack HughesAgenciesFri 23 Oct 2026 12.47 EDTLast modified on Fri 23 Oct 2026 13.50 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleConnor Hellebuyck finally has a new home after the Winnipeg Jets granted the three-time Vezina Trophy-winning goaltender’s trade request in a deal that sent him to theNew Jersey Devilson Friday.The Devils sent center Dawson Mercer, goalie Nico Daws, prospect Alexander Command, forward Nick Bjugstad, a 2029 second-round pick and a 2027 seventh-rounder to Winnipeg for Hellebuyck.American exodus: why do so many US NHL stars want out of Canada?Read moreThe long-awaited blockbuster trade ends months of speculation, a failed bid in June to move the US Olympic gold medal-winner and 2024-25 NHL MVP, and the Jets’ suspension of Hellebuyckfor failing to report to training campin a standoff that required the involvement of the league and the NHL Players’ Association.The 33-year-old Hellebuyck, whobackstopped the US to Olympic goldat the Milan-Cortina Games in February, leaves Winnipeg after spending his entire 11-year career there. Hellebuyck joins Jack Hughes, who scored in overtime of the final to defeat Canada, with the Devils and immediately puts them closer to being Stanley Cup contenders.When training camp opened, new Devils general manager Sunny Mehta said he was very comfortable with the team’s goaltending situation. Since then, Daws and Jake Allen have combined for an .880 save percentage, which ranks 23rd among 32 teams.It was not immediately clear how soon Hellebuyck may be ready to play for his new team. He had been skating in his home state of Michigan while trade talks were ongoing.Hellebuyck has five seasons left on a seven-year contract with an annual salary cap hit of $8.5m.He becomes the latest high-profile Americanto leave Canada for the United States. In June, Ottawa dealt captain Brady Tkachuk to the Florida Panthers, where he joined his brother Matthew. Last December, the Vancouver Canucks traded star defenseman Quinn Hughes, a brother of Jack and teammate Luke, to the Minnesota Wild.The process to trade Hellebuyck became messy, especially after the goalie went public with his request to leave Winnipeg in September. The Jets suspended the goalie for failing to report for camp in a disciplinary move that extended into the season, with Hellebuyck not getting paid.The length of the suspension became an issue, with the league and union determining Hellebuyck would be allowed to rejoin the Jets on Friday. Instead, a move to New Jersey materialized ahead of Winnipeg hosting the outdoor Heritage Classic this weekend.View image in fullscreenConnor Hellebuyck, the three-time Vezina Trophy winner and US Olympic gold medalist, has joined the New Jersey Devils after spending his entire 11-year NHL career with the Winnipeg Jets.Photograph: Charles Krupa/APThe post-Hellebuyck plans went into motion over the summer, with the Jets signing Stuart Skinner in free agency. Winnipeg claimed Clay Stevenson off waivers before the season began, and their combined .907 save percentage is seventh-best in theNHL.The Jets were second-guessed for not dealing Hellebuyck in June, when teams had more options to prioritize salary cap space to make room to acquire the goalie. The Sabres were among the teams expressing interest in Hellebuyck and were preparing to package a deal that included swapping first-round draft picks – Buffalo had the No 4 selection and Winnipeg had the eighth.The challenge for Winnipeg became finding a willing trade partner to acquire a goalie with a high price tag and a lengthy contract well after most teams had set their rosters and had little salary cap space to work with. Another question mark involved Hellebuyck’s age and track record of following regular-season success with a spotty playoff record.After Hellebuyck went 9-8 in leading the Jets to the Western Conference finals in his playoff debut in 2018, he has gone 15-26 since, with the Jets advancing to the second round just twice in their next six playoff appearances. In four first-round exits, Hellebuyck had a combined 5-15 record.The disparity between regular-season and postseason success was evident in 2024-25. Leading Winnipeg to the Presidents’ Trophy and winning the Hart Trophy as MVP, Hellebuyck recorded a career-best 47 wins, then went 6-7 in the playoffs as the Jets were eliminated by Dallas in the second round.With a 345-208-55 regular-season record, Hellebuyck ranks 27th in career wins on the NHL list and fifth among US-born players. Among US-born goalies with 300 or more career starts, his .916 save percentage ranks fourth and his 2.58 goals-against average ranks sixth.Explore more on these topicsNew Jersey DevilsNHLWinnipeg JetsUSA Olympic teamIce hockeyUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: Molly Picklum claims lead in WSL title race with ‘dream’ win in Portugal | Surfing | The Guardian
description: Australian defeats Cailtin Simmers in World Surf League women’s final while Griffin Colapinto scores near-perfect barrel to beat ⁠Gabriel Medina
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Australian defeats Cailtin Simmers in World Surf League women’s final while Griffin Colapinto scores near-perfect barrel to beat ⁠Gabriel Medina
Content: Molly Picklum surfing on her way to victory in the women’s final at the World Surf League’s Rip Curl Pro Portugal at Supertubos Beach.Photograph: Nuno Reisinho/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenMolly Picklum surfing on her way to victory in the women’s final at the World Surf League’s Rip Curl Pro Portugal at Supertubos Beach.Photograph: Nuno Reisinho/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockSurfingMolly Picklum claims lead in WSL title race with ‘dream’ win in PortugalAustralian defeats Cailtin Simmers in World Surf League women’s finalGriffin Colapinto scores near-perfect barrel to beat ⁠Gabriel MedinaReutersFri 23 Oct 2026 18.31 EDTLast modified on Fri 23 Oct 2026 18.47 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAustralia’s reigning world champion Molly Picklum won the Portugal Pro in thumping tubes on Friday, claiming her first victory of the year and ⁠jumping to the top of the rankings with just two events of surfing’s world tour remaining.California’s Griffin Colapinto scored a near-perfect barrel to come from behind and ⁠claim the win over Brazil’s ⁠Gabriel Medina in ​the men’s final, notching up his third victory at the powerful Portuguese beach break of Supertubos.Surfing faces a cultural reckoning as women’s voices grow louder over sexual abuse allegations | Lucy SmallRead morePicklum has had a strong if not spectacular season after winning ⁠her first world title in Fiji last year, but had made only one final and set her sights on securing a win in Portugal ahead of the season finale in Hawaii ⁠in December.“It was a dream of mine to win here,” the 23-year-old said. “Portugal is like the cross between the ​Brazilian energy and Pipeline. Those are two of ‌my favourite things.“I’m really happy to ‌hit my stride at the right time. We work so hard and not many people get to win, but ‌I’m so stoked to get my win this year.”Allow Instagram content?This article includes content provided byInstagram. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content,click 'Allow and continue'.Allow and continueUp against California’s 2024 world champion Caitlin Simmers in the final, Picklum slipped behind in the early exchanges before locking into a deep, overhead tube on her backhand that scored 7.83 out of 10 and gave her the lead. Simmers threaded some nice tubes of her own but ended with a two-wave total of 12.84 to Picklum’s 13.33.Colapinto, 28, has developed a special relationship ‌with the powerful, punchy tubes around the seaside town of Peniche, securing event wins in 2022, 2024 and now 2026.He started strongly in the final, hustling Medina for the first ​wave, pulling into a deep barrel on his forehand and finishing it strongly. He scored an excellent 8.17 and backed it up quickly with a similar wave to pile the pressure on Medina.But Brazil’s three-time world champion responded with an incredible barrel of his own on his backhand, squeezing out when all hope seemed lost, then took the lead with ⁠another long tube.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionNeeding something special, Colapinto found a gem on his backhand, disappearing behind ​the curtain for the entire wave ​and emerging near the packed crowd on ​the beach for a 9.43 out of a possible 10 and a lead he held ​until the clock ran ‌out.“That’s the dream. How ​good were the waves ​out there?” said Colapinto, who climbed to third in the rankings after his win. “The battle with Gabriel was unreal … Portugal has a big place in my heart.“The tour heads next to a new stop in the Philippines before the last event of the year at Pipeline, where 1.5 times points will be on offer.Explore more on these topicsSurfingAustralia sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: NWSL drops controversial criteria around ‘Rodman Rule’ in settlement with NWSLPA | NWSL | The Guardian
description: The terms of the agreement eliminates the previous eligibility requirements, which had ranged from USWNT minutes to appearances on marketability lists
Author: Ella Brockway
Headline: The terms of the agreement eliminates the previous eligibility requirements, which had ranged from USWNT minutes to appearances on marketability lists
Content: Trinity Rodman became the first player to sign under the NWSL’s High Impact Player mechanism earlier this year.Photograph: Kiyoshi Mio/Imagn Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenTrinity Rodman became the first player to sign under the NWSL’s High Impact Player mechanism earlier this year.Photograph: Kiyoshi Mio/Imagn Images/ReutersNWSLNWSL drops controversial criteria around ‘Rodman Rule’ in settlement with NWSLPAAny player will be eligible for High Impact Player statusRequirements had included top 100, marketability listsSides also resolve grievance on Rodman contract refusalElla BrockwayFri 23 Oct 2026 15.25 EDTLast modified on Fri 23 Oct 2026 15.42 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTheNWSLand the NWSL Players Association have reached a settlement to drop the restrictive criteria around the controversial High Impact Player (HIP) rule, allowing any player to earn the league’s highest salaries.The NWSLintroducedthe rule late last year, allowing teams to spend an additional $1m above the salary cap to sign star players. Players with the designation had to meet one of eight criteria, ranging from US national team minutes and Ballon d’Or recognition to NWSL Best XI honors to media lists, includingthe Guardian’s Top 100and a ranking that ordered athletes by marketability.‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from ArsenalRead moreThe NWSLPA opposed the mechanism and filed a grievance, arguing that the classification of players was a violation of federal labor law and the existing collective bargaining agreement. About 100 players had qualified for the designation based on the criteria – a total that, at the time the rule was introduced, included the likes of Trinity Rodman and Sophia Wilson butwould have excludedsuch players as two-time NWSL MVP Sam Kerr and US star Catarina Macario.Under the settlement, which was announced Friday, the eligibility criteria were eliminated. Beginning 1 January 2027, clubs will be able to designate any player as a High Impact Player, so long as their salary equals at least 12% of the base salary cap. The league can also set a limit on the number of HIP players per club.The two sides settled six grievances in total, including one over the rejection of a contract proposal between the Washington Spirit and Rodman. Another involved the league’s footwear policy, which had dictated what brands players could wear during games.“This settlement is certainly evidence of the NWSLPA’s strength and commitment to enforcing the terms of the Collective Bargaining Agreement,” NWSLPA director Meghann Burke toldESPN, which was the first to report news of the settlement.“Disagreements are a natural part of any mature labor relationship, particularly in a league that is growing and evolving as quickly as ours,” NWSL executive vice-president Bill Ordower said in a statement. “What matters is how you work through them. This agreement gives the players, clubs and league greater clarity and certainty moving forward, while protecting the integrity and competitive balance that is fundamental to the NWSL.”The initial version of the HIP Rule was introduced by the league last December. It allowed teams to spend $1m above the salary cap – for the 2026 season, set at $3.7m – to keep star players amida wave of talentdeparting for Europe, where teams are not bound by salary caps.The rule was ratified by the league’s board of governors and went into effect on 1 July. It became known informally as the “Rodman Rule” because its introduction coincided with the Washington Spirit star’sprolonged contract sagathis past offseason.Call it the Rodman Rule or HIP, the NWSL’s new initiative is already impacting rostersRead moreRodman had received lucrative offers from teams in Europe that the Spirit could not have matched under the NWSL’s salary cap rules. In November, before the HIP rule was introduced, the Spiritattemptedto re-sign Rodman to a deal that would have averaged more than $1m annually, but NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman blocked the offer and said it violated the league’s rules because of its backloaded structure. The NWSLPA filed a grievance on Rodman’s behalf, calling the refusal a “flagrant violation” of player free agency rights.Weeks later, the league introduced the HIP rule. Rodmanre-signedwith the Spirit in January on a record deal worth more than $2m annually.The union grievance over the initial refusal of Rodman’s contract remained open after she signed the new contract. While teams are not required to disclose who is signed using the HIP mechanism, several players who would have been eligible under the criteria have since been signed or re-signed by teams in the league, including Denver’s Lindsey Heaps, Orlando’s Barbra Banda and Gotham’s Rose Lavelle.The league will still have the ability to reject contracts for salary cap circumvention, but it must notify the union of the decision and provide an explanation within 72 hours. The league will also be required to provide salary cap and revenue updates to its clubs throughout the year.The settlement also addressed the league’s footwear policy. Throughout this season, some players have received warnings and fines for wearing cleats from brands that were not official sponsors. The league will now honor pre-existing endorsement deals for most players and withdraw previous fines.Explore more on these topicsNWSLWomen's footballUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club
Content: Manchester United's woes: featuring Michael Carrick, Bruno Fernandes, fans and young players such as Shea Lacey.Composite: Guardian Pictures; Shutterstock; Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenManchester United's woes: featuring Michael Carrick, Bruno Fernandes, fans and young players such as Shea Lacey.Composite: Guardian Pictures; Shutterstock; Getty ImagesManchester UnitedChange captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester UnitedThe beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken clubJamie JacksonFri 23 Oct 2026 15.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 23 Oct 2026 15.02 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTake captaincy from Fernandes, then try to sell him and MartínezThe big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor.Carrick delivers 5min 27sec monologue and says he will hold brolly to keep everyone dryRead moreEnsure the players connect with the fansSeven hundred United supporters made the trip to Lombardy and witnessed a horror show in incessant rain as their team folded against Cesc Fàbregas’s side. Yet, as always, the faithful will be there on Sunday desperate to cheer their men on against Bournemouth and beyond. Carrick constantly talks of how fans are the club’s lifeblood but do all of the players feel this? Performances such as that at Como will surely be averted if a base creed citing how fundamental supporters are to United is laid down to the squad by the manager.Play with joy againSir Alex Ferguson’s flying wingers, Sir Matt Busby’s holy trinity of Best, Law, Charlton, the “attack, attack, attack” mentality: none of this is evident currently on the field; part of what Carrick admitted on Friday had been “lost”. What is needed is a return to this tradition, and this team are capable as was evident in the spirit of Carrick’s first game of his second tenure. Then, on 17 January 2026 at Old Trafford, he sent out an XI that went at Manchester City from the opening whistle, gave Pep Guardiola’s men zero time to breathe, and a rousing 2-0 victory sent all of a United stripe home jubilant. This, basically, was Carrick’s side last season, a proposition that played with a bounce that landed in third place. This term the smile has vanished and a prevailing sense of doom has settled over the club – precisely what Carrick had vanquished after the gloom of Ruben Amorim’s final days. Time to restore the cavalier edge.United have suffered, in part, this term owing to Carrick’s drive to move to a more possession-based proposition. The problem is one of the key midfielders recruited to execute this, Youri Tielemans, does not have the legs for a central role, and so has been fielded at 10, while Kobbie Mainoo, who can run an engine room, is injured, and Fernandes’ penchant for running about, out of position, means gaps appear where a ball receiver should be.Give the young players more of a chanceIn Fernandes, Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire, Diogo Dalot, Marcus Rashford, Amad Diallo and Martínez there is a core of long-serving senior players who are not performing. To wake this cadre and freshen the mood from what feels a pervasive staleness, why not blood, more regularly, the younger players? The “play the kids instead” trope can be a cliche but it is a truism for a reason: youth has zero to lose, should run around with a smile and can brighten the darkest of times. Shea Lacey, a nippy wide man, Harry Amass, a promising left-back, and the Fletcher twins, Jack, a clever No 10, and Tyler, a defensive midfielder, are 19 and have 22 appearances between them. None could do worse than those senior players ahead of them.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionGet the attack firingIn seven of their 11 games this season United have scored either a solitary goal or none, a shocking statistic that shows up how dysfunctional the attack is and, as part of the creative collective, the midfield too. United have only 10 goals in seven league outings and in three Champions League games have managed five – four of these against the minnows Sabah. At Como there was, again, zero pattern of play, control and a paucity of chances that has to be a serious concern. This has to change or a relegation fight could be United’s. A more off-the-cuff style, allied to an attacking outlook, would suit Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and others and start menacing teams again as United did when beating City, Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool last year.Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Premier League news: Spurs’ nine injuries ‘normal’, says De Zerbi; ‘emotional control’ keeps Blues red-free | Soccer | The Guardian
description: Tottenham manager insists medical team not to blame as more key players drop out while Alonso happy with Chelsea’s new-found discipline
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Tottenham manager insists medical team not to blame as more key players drop out while Alonso happy with Chelsea’s new-found discipline
Content: Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi faces numerous selection issues at Chelsea when Spurs will attempt to win for only the second time in 42 matches.Photograph: John Walton/PAView image in fullscreenTottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi faces numerous selection issues at Chelsea when Spurs will attempt to win for only the second time in 42 matches.Photograph: John Walton/PAThe talkSoccerPremier League news: Spurs’ nine injuries ‘normal’, says De Zerbi; ‘emotional control’ keeps Blues red-freeTottenham manager insists medical team not to blame as more key players drop out while Alonso happy with Chelsea’s new-found disciplineGuardian writers and agenciesFri 23 Oct 2026 17.30 EDTLast modified on Fri 23 Oct 2026 17.38 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google1.‘Big confidence’ in Tottenham’s injury teamRoberto De Zerbi has insisted Tottenham’s medical staff bears no responsibility for the numerous selection issues he faces against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday where his club will attempt to win for only the second time in 42 matches in all competitions.The head coach has been boosted by the return of Pedro Porro from injury while he reported that Andy Robertson, Omar Marmoush and Dominic Solanke were “good” in light of fitness concerns. De Zerbi had bad news elsewhere, however, saying Destiny Udogie was still out and Tosin Adarabioyo was a doubt.James Maddison did not train for three days after the home win over Coventry on Monday and may not be ready, while caution will remain the watchword with Dejan Kulusevski, who played his first minutes since May 2025 against Frank Lampard’s side. De Zerbi could be without nine players due to injury when the longer-term absentees are factored in, including Lucas Bergvall and Savio. Rodrigo Bentancur is suspended.Spurs appointed a new performance director last season in Dan Lewindon and he oversaw a clutch of new hires in the performance department in July. De Zerbi made the point that the club would make a “total report” on injuries at the end of the season but “so far we can’t say anything bad about the medical staff”.“I am convinced our medical staff this season is high level. I have big confidence because I know how they are working and they are good enough to believe in. We are suffering a normal situation in football.”De Zerbi went into detail on the cases of Porro, Bergvall and Robertson to reinforce his argument. “Pedro won the World Cup with Spain,” he said. “Maybe with the head or body he didn’t recover enough to start this season without a pre-season. He already suffered in the World Cup the muscular problem of the hamstring. He felt it in training and played anyway against Aston Villa [on 29 September] because he pushed to come back before the right time and he suffered another injury. What is the responsibility of the medical staff?“Bergvall turned his knee and felt pain in the first minute against Manchester United [on 10 October]. He finished the game and the day after he felt pain. What is the responsibility of the medical staff? Nothing. Robertson played four games in a row for Scotland [during the recent international window] and after that felt a small problem and did not play in Manchester. He played 65 minutes against Coventry and was fatigued. It’s normal fatigue for a player who played [so much].”On Spurs’s terrible record at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi said: “What is the problem? We didn’t play in the past for Tottenham and I was not the Tottenham coach in the last seasons. We have already many problems and this is not a problem.”David Hytner2.Alonso: ‘We keep calm, don’t lose our heads’Xabi Alonso has said greater emotional control is behind the improvement of Chelsea’s disciplinary record, one that saw them picked up 11 red cards last season.Alonso focused on the problem after becoming manager last summer and has been rewarded with better behaviour from his new side. Chelsea, who can expect a feisty encounter when hosting Tottenham on Saturday evening, have not had a red card this season and showed intelligence when theywon 2-0 at Everton last weekend.“For me it comes a lot with emotional control, with the control of the game,” Alonso said. “If you are focused on what you have to do, you are prepared for what’s going on. Normally you don’t make that many mistakes and don’t overreact to certain situations.“This is a fundamental part of the game, to have that emotional control. The momentum is coming – we keep calm, I don’t lose my head and I don’t get stupid yellow cards, make stupid penalties.”Alonso pointed to Chelsea signing more experienced players last summer. “I think it helps,” he said. “Absolutely. It helps for that composure that you need in certain moments. You have players that sometimes, even during the game, they take a step back to see this is happening and now we need to keep focused and calm.”Stamford Bridge is usually at its loudest when Spurs turn up at a ground where they have not won since 2018. Alonso expects an “electric” atmosphere but admitted that playing with control in the Premier League can be tough when crowds feed off duels and end-to-end football. “It is really difficult,” he said.View image in fullscreenChelsea manager Xabi Alonso has played down the impact of his influence from the touchline: ‘I have from the touchline some kind of input but the real one is from the players.’Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters“To find a total dominance in a game when you are in full control and you have few problems like in other leagues, it’s difficult to find it in the Premier League unless you have become a top, top, top team. That’s why you can’t rest on your laurels when you are 2-0 up.”Alonso played down the impact of his influence from the touchline. “It is people on the pitch,” the Spaniard said. “I can say many things but sometimes I don’t reach [the players], I don’t control. I can do it in advance. I have from the touchline some kind of input but the real one is from the players. Normally the most experienced ones. It’s the ones that feel it.”Chelsea are without Emiliano Martínez after the goalkeeper broke his jaw against Everton. Mike Penders will start and Alonso sees similarities between the young Belgian and his compatriot Thibaut Courtois. “I spoke with Thibaut as well when he was in the World Cup, asking about Mike, and he even said that he could see resemblances with Mike,” Alonso said.Jacob Steinberg3.Go easy on Ngumoha, says IraolaAndoni Iraola has insisted Rio Ngumoha must be allowed to make mistakes and not have his development stifled by “impossible” demands.The 18-year-oldsparkled for Liverpool in their Champions League comebackagainst Villarreal on Tuesday while still adapting to playing on the right wing. It was only a fifth start under Iraola for Ngumoha, who last month became the third-youngest player to make his competitive debut for England, after Wayne Rooney and Jude Bellingham.The Liverpool head coach has described it is a “privilege” to coach the teenager but is wary of too many expectations being heaped on such a young talent.“I feel very lucky to have him but this is a moment when, because he has played well, we cannot straight away put expectations on him super high because it is not fair for him,” Iraola said. “He will still have to make mistakes, he will still have his moments where it is up and down, because this is a natural process that every player goes through.“We cannot straight away put demands on Rio that are impossible to beat. No, we have to help him in this process knowing that he will have good games and probably some games when it is not so good.”Iraola believes Ngumoha’s personality offers reassurance that he will not be unduly affected by the growing attention. The winger has two years remaining on the contract he signed on turning 17 but is expected to be rewarded with a new deal.“I haven’t felt that he’s very affected, positively or negatively, by all the things that are said about him,” Iraola added. “He’s very focused on the football side, on improving his performances and trying to get the things that we need from him. It’s not easy when you are 18 and everyone is talking about you but he knows that what matters is what is happening today in training and the things that he can add to his game. He’s very focused on that.”Liverpool will again be without the injured Dominik Szoboszlai when hosting in-form Brighton on Sunday and Victor Muñoz is doubtful with a knock sustained in last weekend’s win at Brentford.Andy HunterView image in fullscreenThe 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha sparkled for Liverpool in their Champions League comeback against Villarreal on Tuesday.Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA4.Farke faces triple injury blowDaniel Farke has been dealt a blow before Sunday’s Premier League game at Sunderland after revealing Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Anton Stach and Noah Okafor are all injury doubts.Calvert-Lewin, whose fourth league goal of the season earned Leeds a 1-1 home draw against Manchester United last week, and midfielder Stach both sustained foot injuries in that match. Winger Okafor is struggling with a thigh strain and all three players are rated “major doubts” after missing out on team training this week.Farke confirmed Daniel James is in restraint after recovering from his recent injury, while Lukas Nmecha, Harry Wilson and Jean-Mattéo Bahoya will also be hoping to feature. Nmecha has made six league appearances off the bench this season and Farke added: “Overall you have to say for a back-up striker, Lukas has scored I think seven goals last season,” said Farke.“Of course, if he doesn’t play each and every minute due to the fact that Dominic was so outstanding, I think this is a really good record and I would have to say in the last game he looked sharp.”Press Association5.Nothing has changed for us, says ArbeloaAlvaro Arbeloa maintains “nothing has changed” as his Fulham side look to build on a first Premier League win. The Spaniard – who took over as head coach at Craven Cottage in the summer – has come under scrutiny following a testing start to the campaign before easing some of the pressure with a1-0 victory over Hull at Craven Cottage.Fulham come up against another promoted side at Coventry on Saturday and Arbeloa wants his players to continue to show the same focused mindset. “Nothing has changed for us,” Arbeloa said. “When we were not winning games, we believed that we were doing so many things well, and now we have the same targets, so we should come in and try to win a tough game.“Yes, now we have the reward that we were looking for, and now it is another week, another game, so we need to fight again for the win.”Arbeloa added: “When you are working and you are not winning, it is not easy, so everything is easier when you play well, in the way that you want and you win matches. That is the most important thing, and it is very important for your confidence, and I think we deserve it.”Press Association6.Richest clubs face £1.8m bill for regulatorThe highest-earning Premier League clubs will pay up to £1.8m towards the cost of the independent football regulator (IFR) from next summer, but could face paying much higher amounts in the years ahead.The IFR has opened a consultation proposal on the levy needed to fund it, and has projected a total cost to the 116 clubs in the top five divisions of English football of £20.3m in the first year of its licensing regime – 2027-28 – rising to £20.9m in 2028-29. That figure is double the government’s original estimate of £10m a year being required for the IFR.It is thought Premier League clubs will cover around 85% of the total annual IFR costs, though the amount each club repays will be designed to be proportionate to their revenues. The highest-earning clubs will pay up to £1.8m in year one, the IFR said, but it added that most Premier League teams would pay £600,000.However, costs could rise significantly in the future, with the consultation document confirming that set-up costs for the regulator ran to around £45m. Only £1m of that is being recovered in 2027-28, and £2m the year after, leaving some £42m to be recovered over the next eight years. A further £1m of the 2027-28 levy is a contribution to building up reserves for any future litigation costs.David Kogan, the IFR chair, confirmed last week that clubs would ultimately foot the bill for any legal action it may be involved in against Manchester City,depending on the outcome of their Premier League disciplinary case, which could be a significant amount.He said that any legal costs incurred by the IFR in that matter would in the first instance be covered by the government and then recovered from clubs, but stressed that legal action would only be instigated if the advice was that it would succeed, meaning costs could be recovered from the other side.City have been found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules over a nine-season period, but have appealed against the verdict. The IFR has the power to force owners to divest from clubs in cases of serious wrongdoing.The IFR’s media release compared its running costs with the Premier League’s administration costs of more than £200m for the 2024-25 season, a comparison is understood to have caused surprise within the top flight.The Premier League has more than three times the IFR’s staff, generates more than £4bn annually, and its administration costs include all operating expenses plus investments in other areas aimed to help the league grow further, such as the set-up of new production studios. It also includes its legal costs related to the City case and others.The IFR said Championship clubs not in receipt of parachute payments would pay around £45,000 for 2027-28, with clubs in Leagues One and Two paying around £9,000 and £6,000 each. National League clubs would pay around £600 a year each, the IFR said.Richard Monks, the IFR chief executive, said: “I am aware of the £10m figure [originally estimated by the government] and, to be clear, that is not a number we believe reflects either the current financial reality or the task ahead of us. The levy we are proposing today represents a fair and balanced approach and will ensure that most clubs pay around 0.1% of their annual revenues.“We are confident football will see this is a relatively modest investment to help achieve a more sustainable ecosystem which will provide peace of mind for fans, clubs and the communities they serve.”Press AssociationExplore more on these topicsFootballThe talkTottenham HotspurChelseaLiverpoolLeeds UnitedFulhamnewsShareReuse this content

title: Arteta concerned over Saka’s durability as forward faces possible six-week absence | Arsenal | The Guardian
description: Mikel Arteta said of the injured Bukayo Saka: ‘We need to understand how to manage his load,’ while Max Dowman could play against Everton on Saturday
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Mikel Arteta said of the injured Bukayo Saka: ‘We need to understand how to manage his load,’ while Max Dowman could play against Everton on Saturday
Content: Bukayo Saka played a pass against Bayern Munich and then fell to the ground holding his left leg.Photograph: Kai Pfaffenbach/ReutersView image in fullscreenBukayo Saka played a pass against Bayern Munich and then fell to the ground holding his left leg.Photograph: Kai Pfaffenbach/ReutersArsenalArteta concerned over Saka’s durability as forward faces possible six-week absenceArteta: ‘We need to understand how to manage his load’Max Dowman could play against Everton on SaturdayEd AaronsFri 23 Oct 2026 17.33 EDTFirst published on Fri 23 Oct 2026 10.44 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMikel Arteta has expressed concern over Bukayo Saka’s robustness after a series of injuries to the forward in the past year and as he awaits further news on how long he will be out for with a thigh issue.Saka is set for an MRI scanafter limping offin the2-2 draw with Bayern Munichin the Champions League, with Arteta revealing the 25-year-old had “quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury”. Saka will definitely miss Saturday’s game against Evertonand, it is understood, Arsenal fear it could be a grade-two tear that could potentially keep him out for up to six weeks.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBruno Guimarães had sleepless nights before Newcastle exit but hopes for same ‘love’ at ArsenalRead moreSaka missed a large portion of last season due to hamstring, hip and achilles tendon injuries having also been sidelined by another hamstring issue in 2024-25. In total, he has had 11 different injuries since September 2023 and Arteta insisted that he has been trying to ease his workload as a result. “It’s certainly been different in the last year or so,” the Spaniard said when asked if Saka remains robust enough to start every match. “The demands that we are putting on every player are immense. The amount of games, the intensity of those matches, the international competitions, the times as well between games are getting narrower.“Bukayo against Lille [in the Champions League last week] didn’t start the game because we knew what was happening. We have to play three times in less than six days. And especially when the games are so demanding, until the last minute you are there, you are chasing the game, you want to win. The necessity is to win every game, so we know that. So we are preparing the players for those scenarios and we do the best that we possibly can.”Saka missed only three Premier League matches in three seasons between 2021 and 2024 and broke theArsenalclub record by playing in 83 consecutive top-flight games. He is already approaching 300 appearances for the club he joined as a seven-year-old and was rewarded with a lucrative new contract in February that made him one of the highest-paid players in the club’s history.Timber’s touch of class and supersub Saka secure Arsenal win against LilleRead moreAsked whether he feared Saka could suffer from burnout having made his Arsenal debut three months after his 17th birthday, Arteta said: “I don’t have that feeling at all but something we have to be very mindful of is to create the right ecosystem around the player to fulfil his qualities. We really need to understand, whenever he comes back, how we are going to manage his load, what he is capable of to sustain having an impact in the team.”Saka had only three weeks off after the World Cup but Arteta rejected suggestions that he should have been given more We want to pick on something, we will find it, but we won’t know whether it is for that or not. Maybe we needed to load those tendons more during those three weeks? Because if you don’t load the tendons, it becomes a problem. Who knows? I don’t know.”Saka’s absence could hand an opportunity to Max Dowman on Saturday. The 16-year-old has played only nine minutes in the league this season and Arteta feels sure he is ready to make an impact after he became theyoungest goalscorer in Premier League history, against David Moyes’s side in March.“There is something inevitable to go back to that memory and the feeling of the moment. That’s with us, that’s going to stay in that stadium for a long, long time,” said Arteta. “He’s training and every time he’s got a moment to play, he’s showing that he’s a player that is going to impact the game. For sure he’s going to have minutes.”Explore more on these topicsArsenalMikel ArtetaBukayo SakanewsShareReuse this content
