title: Crystal Palace and Newcastle face off with both in search of season kickstart | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Pierre Sage and Matthias Jaissle face some key questions: both were appointed this summer yet form, and results, have proved elusive
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Pierre Sage and Matthias Jaissle face some key questions: both were appointed this summer yet form, and results, have proved elusive
Content: (Left to right) Crystal Palace’s Jean-Philippe Mateta and manager Pierre Sage, the Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle and Sean Steur.Composite: Guardian Pictures; Anadolu/Getty Images; Shutterstock; Every Second Media/Shutterstock; AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreen(Left to right) Crystal Palace’s Jean-Philippe Mateta and manager Pierre Sage, the Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle and Sean Steur.Composite: Guardian Pictures; Anadolu/Getty Images; Shutterstock; Every Second Media/Shutterstock; AFP/Getty ImagesPremier LeagueCrystal Palace and Newcastle face off with both in search of season kickstartPierre Sage and Matthias Jaissle face some key questions: both were appointed this summer yet form, and results, have proved elusiveEd AaronsandLouise TaylorFri 23 Oct 2026 09.36 EDTLast modified on Fri 23 Oct 2026 12.56 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAre the team underperforming?Conceding 17 goals in seven Premier League matches is not exactly the start Pierre Sage or Crystal Palace’s hierarchy would have hoped for. The transition from Oliver Glasner’s counterattacking 3-4-2-1 formation to the Frenchman’s more aggressive approach has exposed massive weaknesses in defence, culminating with last week’s humiliating defeat at Brighton. Palace fansbecame used to success under Glasnerand they are already looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom three. Even their league wins under Sage so far – against Fulham and Nottingham Forest – could have ended in defeat. Something doesn’t seem right in south London.EAThere have been so many arrivals and departures on Tyneside in recent months that it’s too early to say. Any team that sold their three best players – Sandro Tonali, Anthony Gordon and Bruno Guimarães in Newcastle’s case – during the summer would expect a degree of disruption. Eight signings were made, with four aged 20 and under and the others aged 24 and under, and only one (Nico González) had Premier League experience.Throw in a change of managerand an almost entirely new backroom staff and playing style three weeks before the season and teething troubles seem almost inevitable.LTGómez halfway-line wondergoal sparks Brighton’s 5-0 thrashing of sorry Crystal PalaceRead moreHow much pressure is the manager under?Sage issailing extremely close to the windand was warned after the Brighton game that things must improve quickly or he will be shown the door. It is understood that the Palace chair, Steve Parish, has yet to be convinced by the manager who led Lens to the French Cup last season and has demanded improvements in defence. After the creditable Europa League draw with Besiktas in midweek, Sunday’s meeting with Newcastle is crucial to his future. Thomas Frank and Kieran McKenna are likely candidates should Sage get sacked. Ipswich would be due substantial compensation for McKenna despite him leaving Portman Road in the summer, which could be a major hurdle.EAView image in fullscreenAdam Wharton (centre) looks dejected during Crystal Palace’s defeat at Brighton.Photograph: Robbie Hoad/Every Second Media/ShutterstockVery little internally but, externally, the honeymoon is over. Newcastle paid Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ahli £9.5m compensation for Matthias Jaissle, convinced that the 38-year-old German and his “vertical football” were ideal fits. David Hopkinson, the chief executive, and Ross Wilson, the sporting director, are very impressed by Jaissle’s management style, particularly his collaborative approach. They appreciate that Eddie Howe’s successor is new to thePremier League, did not have a proper pre-season and is coping with a raft of injuries. All parties remain sufficiently realistic to predict a season of “ups and downs” but Newcastle’s Saudi Arabian owners crave a return to Europe. Many fans believe Jaissle’s football is old-school, rudimentary long ball with a fancy name, and believe his system and team selections have been flawed. They fear he may be a slave to philosophy.LTHow much responsibility does the manager bear?Palace have looked a shadow of the sidethat won three trophiesin the space of 12 months under Glasner and Sage must take some of the blame. He fell out with Parish after failing to sign several of his preferred targets in the summer, but it was his decision to break up the Adam Wharton-Daichi Kamada axis in central midfield having brought in Quinten Timber on deadline day. While the Dutchman, who missed the game in Turkey due to injury, has provided extra energy and Kamada has excelled in a more advanced role, Wharton has been struggling defensively. Palace looked much more solid when Wharton and Kamada started together against Besiktas – surely Sage will now stick with the partnership that served Glasner so well.EAJaissle’s belief in a gung-ho 4-2-3-1 featuring a classic No 10 is serving him badly at Newcastle, where he does not possess a natural attacking playmaker. It is also leaving González, a holding midfielder, frequently overrun and in need of additional support. With Malick Thiaw and, particularly, Sven Botman struggling in central defence, a switch to a more stable 3-5-2 may be sensible. More importantly, changing the philosophy to a more contain-and-counterattack approach would help camouflage the flaws and make the most of the team’s blistering attacking pace. Jaissle’s high-pressing, attack-minded tactics often appear overly high-risk. His critics fear he may prove to be another Ruben Amorim but Newcastle insiders insist Howe’s successor will prove more flexible than he may seem. Newcastle have not kept a league clean sheet for 13 games, equalling a club record, but six of those came under Howe.LTHow much is beyond the manager’s control?A typically chaotic end to the transfer window left Sage with a bloated squad but insufficient leadership at the back after selling Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea. Axel Disasi’s three-match ban due to a reckless red card against Ipswich, after he arrived on loan from Stamford Bridge along with the promising Italian teenager Honest Ahanor, hasn’t helped. Parish and the sporting director, Matt Hobbs, deserve criticism for not bringing in more experienced replacements, with the latter’s position also thought to be under heavy scrutiny. Sage has also had to deal with unhappy attackers in Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, who made no secret of their desire to leave Selhurst Park in the summer.EAQuite a lot. Given his late arrival, Jaissle had limited influence over Wilson’s eight summer signings. He has, though, apparently swiftly decided that Aladji Bamba (£34m from Monaco) and Bazoumana Touré (£43m from Hoffenheim) are not ready to be thrown into Premier League combat. Similarly, the fleet-footed £51m former Lille forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo looks as if he is going to need time to adjust. Newcastle’s policy of generally recruiting players under 25 dictates the dressing room is a little light on leadership. Meanwhile iIt is hard to say whether the manager’s high-intensity training bears any responsibility for a lengthy injury list, with Anthony Elanga, Tino Livramento and Jacob Ramsey notable absentees.LTskip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenMatias Fernandez-Pardo, seen here rounding Coventry keeper Carl Rushworth but failing to score, will need time to adjust to the Premier League.Photograph: Nick Potts/PAHow important is winning this game?After seeing positive signs against Besiktas, as Mateta scored on his first start since the opening day, three points on Sunday will be crucial for Sage. Yet while Palace haven’t lost to Newcastle at home since November 2020, Jaissle’s side have had extra time to prepare and will present a difficult challenge.EAGiven that Newcastle are 11th it is far from imperative. And yet after ademoralising 4-1 defeat at Coventryand a 1-0 home reverse against Aston Villa, victory would offer much-needed reassurance regarding the team’s potential and boost player confidence, not to mention quieten the social-media noise surrounding Jaissle and his tactics.LTAre thereany reasons for optimism?Palace’s summer net spend of almost £40m in profit was the second lowest in the Premier League behind Aston Villa. They also have American owners who are estimated to be worth a combined £10bn. But Parish revealed last month that he is still looking for extra funding for the new main stand at Selhurst Park, with Woody Johnson, Josh Harris and David Blitzer thought to be open to selling their shares after Palace enlisted Raine Group to seek fresh investment in the club. So there is plenty riding on making sure there is no prospect of being relegated. Sage showed at Lens that he is capable of building a winning team and needs time to do that.EAYes, quite a few. Jaissle, understandably, does not want to overplay the 18-year-old central midfielder Sean Steur but the summer signing from Ajax is a joy to watch, has a wonderful passing range and looks capable of reaching the top. Lewis Hall, the England left-back, looks to be going from strength to strength and is capable of elevating standards. Despite an undoubted dogmatic streak, Jaissle appears intelligent – and humble – enough to learn from his mistakes and make necessary adjustments. Club insiders cite his refreshing willingness to listen. Newcastle also possess several extremely quick attacking players – and, as coaches rarely tire of pointing out: “If you’ve got pace, you’ve got a chance.”LTExplore more on these topicsPremier LeagueCrystal PalaceNewcastle UnitedfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start | Brighton & Hove Albion | The Guardian
description: The German midfielder ‘who can never stand still’ has brought renewed energy to the Seagulls since his return to the club in January
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: The German midfielder ‘who can never stand still’ has brought renewed energy to the Seagulls since his return to the club in January
Content: Pascal Gross was the Premier League’s player of the month for September.Photograph: Charlotte Wilson/Offside/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenPascal Gross was the Premier League’s player of the month for September.Photograph: Charlotte Wilson/Offside/Getty ImagesBrighton & Hove AlbionPascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast startMidfielder ‘who can never stand still’ has brought renewed energy to Seagulls since return to the club in JanuaryEd AaronsFri 23 Oct 2026 07.11 EDTLast modified on Fri 23 Oct 2026 12.39 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMost footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross. Having been part of the Germany squadeliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024, the midfielder entered – and won – a running race.Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor.Gómez halfway-line wondergoal sparks Brighton’s 5-0 thrashing of sorry Crystal PalaceRead moreGross was moving from Brighton to Borussia Dortmund after seven years in the Premier League and reported to his boyhood club for pre-season training days later. Running is an obsession for Gross, as it is for his former teammate James Milner, who revealed last month he was training for a marathon after finally hanging up his boots, and that has shown since he returned for a second spell at the Amex in January for a bargain £1.2m.“I think he’s looking in his free time now: ‘Where can I run a race?’ Because he will never stand still,” joked Brighton’s head coach, Fabian Hürzeler, after the 35-year-old scored the opening goal in a3-0 victory over Arsenal last month. “ During the off-season he’s never the person who can lay on the beach for several hours and do nothing. He always needs to do something.”Given that Gross has this season racked up an average distance of more than 11.5km per match and has covered the third-most ground of any player in the Premier League, it is no surprise Hürzeler has compared his compatriot to a good wine: “The older the wine gets, the better it gets.”That analysis is borne out by the rest of his statistics this season as Brighton have emerged as challengers for Champions League qualification, at the very least, before Sunday’s game at Liverpool. Not only has Gross, the Premier League’s player of the month for September, contributed a combined seven goals and assists, he is in the top five for several other metrics such as big chances created (six), chances created from open play (14) and line-breaking passes leading to a goal (three). In a team that have scored the fourth-most goals (23) in Premier League history after seven games, Gross has been the standout performer.View image in fullscreenPascal Gross (in white) up against Jablonec's Matej Polidar in the Conference League. The match finished 0-0.Photograph: David W Cerny/Reuters“Sometimes he’s just one step ahead than his opponent,” said Hürzeler, who is understood to have been instrumental in bringing back Gross. “He might not be the quickest player, but he can be the quickest in the head and sometimes being the quickest in the head is very helpful. No one expected that it would be this good. But it also shows that he still has this capacity in his body.”At a club where experience is valued despite Hürzeler being the youngest permanent manager in the Premier League’s history, insiders describe Gross as the perfect role model for some of Brighton’s younger players. Charalampos Kostoulas has scored three goals in his past four league matches and the 19-year-old Greece striker is clearly thriving alongside the man who is approaching 300 appearances for the club. Diego Gómez, the dynamic Paraguayan who scored a goal-of-the-season contender against Crystal Palace that will go down in Brighton folklore, the homegrown talent Jack Hinshelwood and the midfield linchpin Yasin Ayari are others benefiting from his vast experience, as is Hürzeler.Gross managed 75 Brighton goals and assists after joining from Ingolstadt in 2017 in the summer when Brighton were promoted. His departure for Dortmund, a year after his first Germany cap, was to fulfil a boyhood dream but there was always something drawing Gross – who wears a long-sleeve shirt owing to a grass allergy – back to the club where he is known as theKaiser.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBrighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan WilsonRead more“It was really difficult,” Gross said of his Brighton exit. “Only something really special got me out of here. There were a couple of other options [before returning], but Brighton was always the priority. I just stayed in touch with all the lads over the time away. Maybe you watch less of the games or you don’t stay in touch as much any more, it gets less and less. But it never really did.”Gross retiring from international football after the World Cup has also been to Brighton’s benefit. His status as a club legend was augmented by delivering the free-kick that Palace’s Jaydee Canvot headed into his own net during the 5-0 humiliation on Sunday. That was the third game in a row in which Gross has provided an assist and he has an opportunity to become the oldest player to make it four since Chelsea’s Gianfranco Zola in December 2002.The trip to Anfield continues a gruelling run of five away fixtures in a row. Brighton drew at the Czech club Jablonec on Thursday in the Conference League and after Sunday they go to Manchester City twice in four days – the first in the Carabao Cup – before heading to Spain to play Getafe. It will test Brighton’s mettle after their spectacular start. Hürzeler can count on Gross – who has started every game in all competitions – to last the course.Explore more on these topicsBrighton & Hove AlbionfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Slegers and misfiring Arsenal badly need a result in WSL north London derby | Arsenal Women | The Guardian
description: Gunners’ title hopes have seemingly evaporated and their under-pressure head coach faces her latest test against Spurs on Saturday
Author: Tom Garry
Headline: Gunners’ title hopes have seemingly evaporated and their under-pressure head coach faces her latest test against Spurs on Saturday
Content: Renée Slegers (in tracksuit) believes Arsenal Women’s form will recover when they take care of certain ‘details and margins’.Photograph: Ed Sykes/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenRenée Slegers (in tracksuit) believes Arsenal Women’s form will recover when they take care of certain ‘details and margins’.Photograph: Ed Sykes/Action Images/ReutersArsenal WomenSlegers and misfiring Arsenal badly need a result in WSL north London derbyGunners’ title hopes have seemingly evaporated and their under-pressure head coach faces her latest test against Spurs on SaturdayTom GarryFri 23 Oct 2026 07.58 EDTLast modified on Fri 23 Oct 2026 11.03 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIt says much about Arsenal’s predicament that the team who have conceded 12 goals in two games are not the side whose head coach is under most pressure before a north London derby. Tottenham, four points above their neighbours before Saturday’s meeting, may have been humbled in consecutive Women’s Super League matches but all eyes are on Renée Slegers.Arsenal are winless in five WSL matches for the first time, and the most decorated club in English women’s football desperately need a turning point. Theirfailure to beat Birmingham at homelast Saturday, dropping points against a promoted side for the second time this season, again demonstrated the team’s inability to convert possession into goals. They increasingly look like a team stuck in Groundhog Day.WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on recordRead moreThe Arsenal hierarchy are understood to remain behind Slegers, but for how long? The answer may hinge on Saturday lunchtime’s result. However much goodwill the Dutchwoman gained forguiding Arsenal to Champions League glory in May 2025, the simple truth is, it is unacceptable for a club with one of the biggest budgets in the world to be 12 points behind the leaders after six games.That gap is why the draw with Birmingham not only pretty much extinguished Arsenal’s title hopes but also burned a hole in their secondary domestic objective – Champions League qualification. The unthinkable prospect of failure appears a genuine possibility: they are nine points adrift of third-placed London City. Arsenal need a derby win on Saturday but also a winning run to reverse the slide, and there is little evidence to suggest such a turnaround is close.Arsenal have the worst shot conversion rate in the league (4.1%) and, according to Stats Perform, the third-worst shooting accuracy (30.6%) and third-lowest average xG per shot (0.09) despite averaging over 60% possession. Slegers’s persistence in deploying Alessia Russo – widely regarded as one of Europe’s best No 9s – in the No 10 role has baffled supporters and commentators alike. Russo has scored more WSL goals against Tottenham (eight) than any other player so Saturday’s game may be the perfect moment for that to change.View image in fullscreenArsenal’s Alessia Russo and Caitlin Foord wheel away after a goal against Tottenham in February 2025 – however, Russo has not flourished as a No 10 this season.Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/ReutersArsenal have struggled against low blocks for a number of seasons, though, so not all fault lies at Slegers’s door. Nonetheless, the 37-year-old was substantially backed in the summer, with Arsenal enjoying perhaps their strongest transfer window in recent memory. So far though they have looked confounded tactically, bruised mentally and lacking the self-belief to grab a game by the scruff of its neck.Asked if she was surprised to still be in her job, Slegers said: “That’s not something I think about. It’s about, ‘where are we as a group?’ and ‘what are we working towards?’ It’s absolutely not what we expected [our recent results] or what we wanted. But I’m in the here and now, and we are preparing for the north London derby. We have the group together. Everyone is going in the same direction and the fuel and motivation is sky high, because of the fans that will be there for us. That’s where my focus will be.”Asked how imperative it is that Arsenal climb back up into a Champions League place this season, Slegers added: “Of course that’s in the back of our heads, but what we need right now is to get back to winning ways. We can only do that with the next game in front of us so that’s why the next game in front of us is the most important right now.”Slegers has maintained after last weekend’s draw that Arsenal will recover when they fix some “details and margins”. Perhaps taking on a Tottenham side who have become only the second team in history to concede six or more goals in consecutive WSL games is the perfect opportunity.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“It is a little bit of game intelligence and smartness in moments,” said the Spurs head coach, Martin Ho, insisting he is not worried about his team’s defending in the long-term. “There have been certain aspects that, collectively, players and staff, we were not happy with in certain moments, and we have to make sure we correct them. At the moment we’re getting heavily punished for some small errors with the ball that we’re making.”The Englishman also only had praise for Arsenal’s qualities when speaking on Friday morning. “If you try and underestimate a team with Arsenal’s quality you’re in for trouble,” he said. Asked about Arsenal’s poor run, Ho added: “Arsenal aren’t a bad side. Their possession stats are probably the highest in the league, alongside Manchester City. Their goalscoring chances and touches in the opposition box are very, very high. They have world-class players.”Last season’s runners-up do have world-class players but it is high time for them to play like a cohesive team.Explore more on these topicsArsenal WomenTottenham Hotspur WomenWomen's Super LeagueWomen's footballfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!  | Soccer | The Guardian
description: In today’s Football Daily: anticipating mischief on Sunday night
Author: Rob Smyth
Headline: In today’s Football Daily: anticipating mischief on Sunday night
Content: Is José Mourinho eyeing mischief?Photograph: Violeta Santos Moura/ReutersView image in fullscreenIs José Mourinho eyeing mischief?Photograph: Violeta Santos Moura/ReutersFootball Daily newsletterSoccerMourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!Rob SmythFri 23 Oct 2026 11.25 EDTLast modified on Fri 23 Oct 2026 12.00 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMOU AND WHOSE ARMY?Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jrdoesn’t have a body doubleand Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced theirBe Ready campaignon Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from ournews story:“Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.”War’s a comin’, in other words, so you’d better buy some tomato soup (10 tins of), mushroom soup (eight tins of, for consumption cold) and ice cream (vanilla, one large tub of). Here’s where it gets interesting. The government released their three-day survival plan on Thursday afternoon, three days before the event most likely to cause World War III: José Mourinho’s first Clásico since 2013. Barcelona meet Real Madrid at the Camp Nou on Sunday and suddenly the government are telling us we may need to hunker down. Coincidence? We think not!OK, OK. Coincidence? We think so! José may be the most charismatic baddie since Dirty Den’s most recent death, but not even he is capable of starting the geopolitical answer to El Clásico. Sunday’s match will spark a form of global conflict, even if it’s just a load of strangers caterwauling at each other on the internet rather than talking to their children, reading a book or practising any of the gazillion behaviours that would make their lives and the world a better place.Mourinho’s relationship with Barcelonacould fill a book, never mind a teatime email. Thereislove lost, but it’s decades since it went missing. These days they can’t stand the thought of each other, never mind the sight. There is an argument (NB: Football Daily doesn’t actually want to argue) that Mourinho’s greatest achievement in football, apart from finishing second with Manchester United in 2017-18, was to take a La Liga title off probably the greatest club side of all time. He also drove Pep Guardiola into a sabbatical – but that, and the Realpolitik of the Bernabéu dressing-room, took so much out of Mourinho that he has never been the same since that triumphant 2011-12 season.The Camp Nou was the venue for Mourinho’s “most beautiful defeat” (you know the one, when not even a good hosing could douse his celebrations) andhis most humiliatingdefeat a few months later. He can’t afford any kind of defeat on Sunday: Madrid are six points behind Barcelona, who have won all nine league games, scoring 39 goals in the process. But Mourinho’s team have scored four goals in each of their last three matches and, even in the absence of the suspended Vinícius Jr , have attacking threats galore. And whatever the result, Mourinho’s post-match press conference will be must-see TV.The match kicks off on Sunday evening, but only if you take these things literally. For Mourinho, it began the moment he was asked a question about it. He has had the face on all week because, well, wouldn’t you if you were treated like this? Barcelona played 24 hours earlier than Madrid in Bigger Cup, an open goal for conspiracy theorists and performative underdogs. “We’re pushing ahead,” he said. “At the moment, we’re missing out on 24 hours of rest, but we’re moving forward.” So is Football Daily, to the supermarket to get some urgent shopping. We’ll Be Ready for Sunday – not with 72 hours of essential supplies, but with a month’s worth of popcorn.LIVE ON BIG WEBSITEJoin Scott Murray at 8pm (BST) for red-hot Premier League updates on Ipswich Town 0-0 Nottingham Forest.QUOTE OF THE DAY“I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and for everyone else to stay dry. You know, that’s the position I’m in, and it’s a privileged position” – Michael Carrick delivers anear six-minute monologuedefending Manchester United’s values in which he veered close to painting a picture of himself as being akin to another former Middlesbrough manager who once held a brolly while watching his team fail.View image in fullscreenSteve McClaren: a reminder.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianFOOTBALL DAILY LETTERSdouble quotation markWould it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, Citywouldmight get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh.double quotation markLike all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recentpiecein The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis.double quotation markMay I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee.If you have any, please send letters tothe.boss@theguardian.com.Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Justin Kavanagh. title: Cheltenham’s racing return provides romance over jumps and 20-1 shock | Horse racing | The Guardian
description: Kingofthefrontier was a surprise winner of the Sharp Novice Hurdle as Cheltenham held its first meeting since March
Author: Greg Wood
Headline: Kingofthefrontier was a surprise winner of the Sharp Novice Hurdle as Cheltenham held its first meeting since March
Content: Conor O'Farrell on board Kingofthefrontier after winning the Sharp Novices' Hurdle at Cheltenham.Photograph: David Davies/PAView image in fullscreenConor O'Farrell on board Kingofthefrontier after winning the Sharp Novices' Hurdle at Cheltenham.Photograph: David Davies/PAHorse racingCheltenham’s racing return provides romance over jumps and 20-1 shockOutsider Kingofthefrontier wins Sharp Novices’ HurdleTrainer John Dawson gets better of Dan SkeltonGreg WoodFri 23 Oct 2026 15.32 EDTLast modified on Fri 23 Oct 2026 15.47 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe jumping game increasingly resembles the Flat when it comes to the concentration of racing power in ever fewer trainers’ hands, but the opening day of Cheltenham’s new season –the first, in fact, since Gold Cup day in March– brought a reminder that romance has not been drained entirely from the winter code.Dan Skelton, who dethroned Willie Mullins to become the new champion over jumps last season, had already trained 115 winners in the current campaign before racing on Friday, nearly halfway towards Martin Pipe’s all-time record of 243. John Dawson, by contrast, had sent out a total of six winners from his yard in North Yorkshire since May 2023.Cheltenham jumps into action after fixing its troublesome holeRead moreHowever, it was Dawson’s Kingofthefrontier, a 20-1 outsider and only the trainer’s third runner at the home of jumping, who led the field home in the Grade Two Sharp Novices’ Hurdle, with Skelton’s Cooltobecareless, the 13-8 favourite, only third. The winner was nearer last than first turning in but showed an impressive turn of foot to run out a two-and-a-quarter length winner from Nicky Henderson’s Planters Punch.Dawson rode into the famous winner’s enclosure aboard Sine Nomine after the Hunters’ Chase at the festival meeting here in March 2024, but his firstCheltenhamwinner as a trainer was an even better moment in what is still a young racing career.“We’ve always loved him since the word go,” Dawson said. “I just felt we had a horse to come and have a go with.He’s still got a lot to learn and the way he went through the race, Conor [O’Farrell, his jockey] said he was a bit stumbly and he had to balance him a couple of times. But speed wasn’t a problem for me, he was always going to have enough boot to get there, and he picked up really well.“He’s actually a little bit horse-shy and when that big horse of Dan Skelton’s came running towards him, I think he was edging away from him, but he’ll learn a lot from that and he could still be anything.”Dawson and Kingofthefrontier’s owner, George Critchley, opted to run in Friday’s Grade Two feature event in preference to a novice handicap hurdle at Carlisle.“He’d never disappointed us,” Dawson said. “George puts a lot into the game, I wanted to bring him here and I thought he had a horse good enough to do it. I just can’t believe it came off.We’re ambitious [but] we only want the horses to have a go with and hopefully we’ve showcased ourselves [today] to do that. I don’t want to be a massive Dan Skelton in numbers, but I just want real quality.”Irish stables have been dominant at the festival meeting in March in recent seasons and Gordon Elliott is already looking ahead to a possible run in the Grand Annual Handicap Chase for Bowensonfire after the six-year-old’s win in the card’s two-mile novice chase.View image in fullscreenBowensonfire ridden by Jack Kennedy on the way to winning the Novices’ Chase.Photograph: David Davies/PABowensonfire was the first leg of a double for Elliott, completed when Cosmos D’Ainay took a novice hurdle later on the card, while Cian Collins sent out a third winner for Ireland on the day when Brandt, at 10-1, took the final race on the card.Quick GuideGreg Wood's Saturday tipsShowDoncaster12.55 Ancient State 1.30 MingleSouthwell4.24 Blake’s Monarch 5.00 Almaty Star 5.30 Raysham 6.00 Ring Of Music 6.30 Geometry 7.00 Lili Marleen 7.30 Gladiadora 8.00 Crystal Dark 8.30 He’s An AngelWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Breacher can provide Futurity Trophy valueAidan O’Brien and Andrew Balding field four of the seven runners in Saturday’s Futurity Trophy at Doncaster, the final Group One of the British season, but the focus on their neck-and-neck tussle for the trainers’ title could mean that the improvingBreacher(1.30) sets off at a value price on ground that promises to suit.William Muir and Chris Grassick’s colt has progressed by the run in three starts to date over seven furlongs, while also looking sure to thrive at middle-distances next season.Cracksman, his sire, was at his best with some cut in the ground and a demanding mile on heavy going could well see Breacher outrun his early odds of around 10-1.Doncaster 12.55:Ancient Stateseems to save his best form for this track and trip and has been dropped 1lb since finishing around one-and-a-half lengths behind the winner at Ascot last time.Cheltenham 1.10:Ben Pauling has his string in excellent form and the returningAs Legends Have Itis an interesting contender at around 8-1. He has gone well fresh in the past, remains fairly weighted on his winning form at the end of last season and his prominent run-style is ideal for this track and trip.Cheltenham 1.45:Olly Murphy’sRoad To Wembley– part-owned by Sir Alex Ferguson – was better than the bare result when fourth on his handicap debut at Worcester in September and should appreciate this move up to three miles.Doncaster 2.05: Bengal Tiger’s 12-length win in a maiden at Naas last time was backed up by an excellent time and he should handle this step up to Listed company without too much fuss.Cheltenham 2.20:James Owen’s string remains in strong form whatever the season or code andIdaho Fireposted a new career best at Uttoxeter last time out – a performance that suggests he could cope with a subsequent 10lb hike in the weights.Cheltenham 2.55:With further rain expected before Saturday’s card,Katate Dori’s form when second over track and trip off a 3lb higher mark in January looks as strong as anything on offer.Cheltenham 3.30:Four of the seven runners in this four-year-old event were in the field for the Triumph Hurdle at the festival and whileIndian Riverwas only 10th, he finished third in the equivalent event at Aintree. title: Wallaroos complete Scotland sweep as retiring Smith gets standing ovation despite red | Australia women's rugby union team | The Guardian
description: Australia completed a three-game sweep over Scotland with a 38-31 win in a spicy contest that featured biting accusations and a string of yellow cards
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Australia completed a three-game sweep over Scotland with a 38-31 win in a spicy contest that featured biting accusations and a string of yellow cards
Content: Cecilia Smith receives a guard of honour from her Wallaroos teammates. The centre was sent off in the final game before her retirement.Photograph: Lukas Coch/AAPView image in fullscreenCecilia Smith receives a guard of honour from her Wallaroos teammates. The centre was sent off in the final game before her retirement.Photograph: Lukas Coch/AAPAustralia women's rugby union teamWallaroos complete Scotland sweep as retiring Smith gets standing ovation despite redWomen’s rugby union: Australia 38-31 ScotlandCecilia Smith ‘sorry’ for red card on final Wallaroos gameAustralian Associated PressFri 23 Oct 2026 12.49 EDTLast modified on Fri 23 Oct 2026 17.52 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Wallaroos completed their three-game sweep over Scotland with a 38-31 win on Friday in a spicy contest that featured biting accusations and a string of yellow cards.Australia produced plenty of classy moments in Canberrabut again lacked discipline in tackles and around the ruck to keep the tourists in it. The hosts received four yellow cards, with the retiring centre Cecilia Smith earning two of those to finish her 34-Test career on a red.Son of Wallabies great named in spring tour squad as Les Kiss turns to new facesRead moreScotland had two players sent to the sin bin and it could have been far uglier if the Wallaroos centre Georgina Friedrichs’ accusations of biting had been verified on review. But the officials saw no evidence and there were no bite marks on Friedrich’s forearm, so the referee waved the complaints away.The Australian prop Eva Karpani was shown a yellow card for a high shot in her milestone game on her 50th cap, while the impressive teenage fly-half Waiaria Ellis was also sent to the sin bin for slowing down a Scottish charge late in the first half.The win came as a relief for the retiring pair Emily Chancellor and Smith, with the latter smiling as she received a standing ovation despite being sent off. “I’m really sorry about that, just wanted to go out with a bang I guess,” Smith said as she embraced her daughter, Ruby, after the match. “She’s been there since day one,” said Smith of her daughter. “Having her there at trainings, camps, on the sideline, means so much and I just want to be that role model and show you can do anything if you put your mind to it and put the hard work in.”A teary Chancellor, former captain and two-time World Cup member, signed off with a win in her 42nd Test after making her debut in 2018. “It’s created so much opportunity for me, so much purpose in my life. I love these girls and what we play for,” she said. “I love what this game has given us: travel the world with great people and create opportunity. You can’t be what you can’t see.”View image in fullscreenSiokapesi Palu makes a break through the Scotland defence to score a try.Photograph: Lukas Coch/AAPVictory for Australia followed wins in Sydney and Edinburgh against Scotland. The Wallaroos are now out of action until the side transitions to a full-time operation next year under their new coach, Sione Fukofuka, who has previously coached Scotland.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe BreakdownThe latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewedEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAustralia led 14-0 early but trailed 17-14 at half-time after a string of penalties led to three successive Scottish tries. The Wallaroos regained the ascendancy and surged back ahead 38-24 when the captain, Siokapesi Palu, finished a long-range effort. But after losing Karpani and then Smith, Scotland surged back into the match, although they were unable to find the match-tying converted try on the final play.Explore more on these topicsAustralia women's rugby union teamScotland women's rugby union teamWomen's rugby unionRugby unionnewsShareReuse this content

title: F1 crown in reach for Kimi Antonelli at bumpy Austin circuit drivers insist is ‘unacceptable’ | Formula One | The Guardian
description: Kimi Antonelli could clinch the Formula One drivers’ title for Mercedes at the US Grand Prix in Austin, where the bumpy track is causing disquiet on the grid
Author: Giles Richards
Headline: Kimi Antonelli could clinch the Formula One drivers’ title for Mercedes at the US Grand Prix in Austin, where the bumpy track is causing disquiet on the grid
Content: Kimi Antonelli at the Circuit of the Americas. ‘It’s the same mindset I’ve had all year,’ he said. ‘One race at a time.’Photograph: Stefano Facchin Photography/Alessio Morgese/SPP/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenKimi Antonelli at the Circuit of the Americas. ‘It’s the same mindset I’ve had all year,’ he said. ‘One race at a time.’Photograph: Stefano Facchin Photography/Alessio Morgese/SPP/ShutterstockFormula OneF1 crown in reach for Kimi Antonelli at bumpy Austin circuit drivers insist is ‘unacceptable’Mercedes youngster could become youngest title winnerMax Verstappen says bumpy track makes drivers ‘suffer’Giles Richardsin AustinFri 23 Oct 2026 18.07 EDTFirst published on Fri 23 Oct 2026 06.34 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Formula One world championship is within reach forKimi Antonelliat the US Grand Prix in Austin this weekend. But while the young Italian approaches the race ­intending simply to have fun, there is disquiet among other ­drivers about the potential long-term health ­dangers posed by the state of the Texas circuit.The 20-year-old Antonelli will become Formula One’s youngest world champion if he claims the title at the Circuit of the Americas on Sunday, eclipsing Sebastian Vettel’s record from 2010, when the German driver was 23 and Antonelli was four. It is an outside chance, as the Italian has acknowledged. He must win while needing his rivals to endure a poor day. His Mercedes teammate George Russell would have to finish outside the top eight and Ferrari’sLewis Hamiltonoutside the top four.Lewis Hamilton aims to extend career till early 2030s so he can race in African Grand PrixRead moreNonetheless, while Antonelli knows the title race is in effect over, he is keeping the cool head that has brought him to this point with such alacrity. The Mercedes ship, helmed by his race engineer Pete Bonnington, who was alongside Hamilton for his six titles with the team, is steady as she goes.“We had a meeting with Bono this morning and we said: ‘Just have fun,’” Antonelli said. “It’s the same mindset I’ve had all year. One race at a time. Just try to do the best I can every race weekend, and then we’ll see.”After a tricky rookie season last year, Antonelli has adapted remarkably quickly to competing at the front of the grid. But as he seeks to close out the title, he feels able to draw on previous experience.“Formula One is different because the pressure is a lot bigger than in anything else,” he added. “The competition is a little bit higher as well because you’re racing with 21 of the best drivers in the world. But when you fight for championships in karting and junior series, the mindset is very similar in the way you approach races and the way you think.”Going into the weekend, however, the circuit has drawn unusually severe criticism from drivers. The race was first held in 2012 and the circuit has a contract until 2034. It has become hugely popular, with sold-out crowds, but the track has come under intense scrutiny.It is built on marshland and the bumps caused by the ground beneath the track have been condemned as potentially harmful, with the uneven surface forcing impacts into the base of the drivers’ spines.Max Verstappen, Red Bull’s four-time world champion, said: “The bumps are unacceptable. Over time they’ve been grinding a little bit here and there but it’s just putting a plaster on the big problem. You need to really fully open up the track. That costs a lot of money and time but that’s the only way to get rid of it because these bumps are not natural and they are out of control.“From the checks that I’ve done from my spine, the bottom end doesn’t look that great. I know that’s part of racing. I know that can be part of sport, but it’s also further damage from the cars that we had the last few years. If we continue with finding this acceptable to drive on, then you are going to suffer with that much more.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |FortnightlySign up toThe HotspotA new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisisEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionVerstappen’s opinion was echoed by the defending world champion, Lando Norris, who is frustrated that drivers’ concerns are not being ­listened to. “It’s pretty bad,” he said. “There’s a lot of places I need to take headache tablets before I go out simply because it’s so bumpy and you’re hitting your head pretty hard against the headrest because of the bumps. So it’s certainly not a nice thing. There’s not much we can do. I mean, we complain about it, it’s stuff we’ve brought up many, many times but there’s only so much we can ­complain about things.”In first practice at the Circuit of the Americas, Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc topped the timesheets from Verstappen, with Lando Norris third for McLaren and Russell and Antonelli in fourth and fifth. Ferrari had brought their final swathe of upgrades to the race and on the early showing they had found some extra pace.In the afternoon running Leclerc was once more on top, four hundredths clear of Antonelli in second. Verstappen was in third, from Hamilton in fourth.Explore more on these topicsFormula OneFormula One 2026Kimi AntonelliMotor sportUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content
